title: OSDL Component Library Definition
description: Describes a component library: the set of component types a plugin contributes, including their ports, parameter schemas, observable state, and emitted events. Tools derive palettes, parameter forms, validation, and documentation from this document; it is the contract between an engine plugin and every OSDL-aware tool.

$schema.description: Optional URI of the OSDL library JSON Schema, for editor tooling.

osdl.description: Version of the OSDL specification this library definition conforms to.

namespace.description: The type-name prefix this library owns, e.g. `des` for `des.queue`. Namespaces are globally unique by convention; `core`, `des`, `abm`, and `sd` are reserved for the standard libraries.

version.description: Semantic version of the library definition.

name.description: Local type name. The full type is `<namespace>.<name>`.

description.description: Required. The semantic contract of this component type, written for humans and language models alike.

category.description: Palette grouping hint for visual editors.

ports.description: The ports every instance of this type exposes. May be empty for components referenced only via expressions (e.g. `sd.auxiliary`).

params.description: A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) that validates the `params` object of instances of this type (phase-two validation). MAY reference value definitions from the core schema, e.g. `https://osdl.dev/schemas/0.1/osdl.schema.json#/$defs/numericValue`.

state.description: Observable state variables, addressable as `<componentId>.<stateId>` in outputs and expressions.

emits.description: Event types instances of this component emit onto the simulation event stream.

kind.description: What the port carries: entities under the custody protocol, immutable message payloads, or typed scalar values. Connections must join ports of the same kind.

multiple.description: Whether more than one connection may attach to this port.

payload.description: A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) describing the event payload.
